description: The individual variable-step and fixed-step solvers selectable in the Solver pane, the key model configuration parameters for tolerances, step size, zero crossings, algebraic loops, tasking, simulation modes, Fast Restart and external mode, and the remaining Configuration Parameters panes with their get_param/set_param names.

tools.name: ode45
tools.description: Variable-step explicit Runge-Kutta (4,5) solver based on the Dormand-Prince pair. It is the recommended first choice for nonstiff continuous models and the solver most 'auto' selections resolve to.

parameters.name: RelTol / AbsTol
parameters.description: Error tolerances controlling step size (defaults 1e-3 and auto).

parameters.name: MaxStep / MinStep / InitialStep
parameters.description: Step-size bounds, all 'auto' by default.

tools.notes: If ode45 takes very small steps for a long time the model is probably stiff; switch to ode15s, ode23t or ode23tb. Use the Solver Profiler to diagnose.

tools.name: ode23
tools.description: Variable-step explicit Runge-Kutta (2,3) Bogacki-Shampine solver. Can be more efficient than ode45 at crude tolerances and in the presence of mild stiffness.
tools.notes: Lower-order: needs more steps than ode45 for tight tolerances.

tools.name: ode113
tools.description: Variable-step, variable-order Adams-Bashforth-Moulton PECE multistep solver. Efficient at tight tolerances and when derivative evaluations are expensive, for smooth nonstiff problems.
tools.notes: As a multistep method it restarts after discontinuities, so it performs poorly in models with frequent zero crossings or events.

tools.name: ode15s
tools.description: Variable-step, variable-order implicit solver using numerical differentiation formulas (NDFs), for stiff systems. The usual choice when ode45 is extremely slow because of widely separated time constants.

parameters.name: MaxOrder
parameters.description: Maximum NDF order, 1-5 (default 5); lower orders are more stable.

parameters.name: SolverJacobianMethodControl
parameters.description: How the solver Jacobian is computed ('auto', sparse/full perturbation or analytical).

tools.notes: Handles DAEs from Simscape and Algebraic Constraint blocks of index 1.

tools.name: ode23s
tools.description: Variable-step one-step implicit solver based on a modified second-order Rosenbrock formula. Efficient for stiff problems at crude tolerances where ode15s is not effective.
tools.notes: Recomputes the Jacobian every step, which is expensive for large models.

tools.name: ode23t
tools.description: Variable-step implicit solver implementing the trapezoidal rule with a free interpolant. Suited to moderately stiff problems that need a solution without numerical damping, and to DAEs.
tools.notes: Auto solver selection picks ode23t for many models with DAE (Simscape) content.

tools.name: ode23tb
tools.description: Variable-step implicit TR-BDF2 solver (trapezoidal rule followed by a second-order backward differentiation step). Efficient for stiff systems at crude tolerances and commonly used for Simscape Electrical models.
tools.notes: Provides numerical damping, which suppresses artificial ringing from switching events.

tools.name: odeN
tools.description: Nonadaptive variable-step solver: it integrates with a fixed-step formula and does not adjust the step for error control, but varies the step to land on sample times and zero crossings. It combines fixed-step cost predictability with accurate event location.

parameters.name: ODENIntegrationMethod
parameters.description: 'ode1', 'ode2', 'ode3' (default), 'ode4', 'ode5', 'ode8', 'ode14x' or 'ode1be'.

parameters.name: MaxStep
parameters.description: Nominal step size.

tools.notes: Useful to preview how a model will behave with a fixed-step solver while keeping zero-crossing detection.

tools.name: daessc
tools.description: Variable-step solver that computes model states by solving systems of differential-algebraic equations directly; designed for robust simulation of Simscape physical networks.
tools.notes: Available with Simscape products. Often more robust than ode15s/ode23t for highly nonlinear physical models.

tools.name: VariableStepAuto
tools.description: Automatic solver selection ('auto' in the dialog): Simulink inspects the model at compile time and chooses a solver (typically ode45, ode23t, ode15s, daessc or discrete) and step settings. FixedStepAuto is the fixed-step counterpart.
tools.example:
set_param(mdl, 'Solver', 'VariableStepAuto', 'MaxStep', 'auto');
out = sim(mdl);   % the solver actually selected is shown in the status bar and Diagnostic Viewer
tools.notes: Default for new models. Check the chosen solver in the Diagnostic Viewer or the bottom status bar.

tools.name: FixedStepDiscrete
tools.description: Solver for models with no continuous states: it only advances time to the next sample hit. VariableStepDiscrete is the variable-step version, which skips time between hits and supports zero crossings of discrete signals.
tools.notes: Simulink reports an error if the model contains continuous states. Typical for controller models intended for code generation.

tools.name: ode1
tools.description: Fixed-step explicit Euler method: the cheapest and least accurate fixed-step solver. ode2 (Heun) is the next order up.
tools.notes: Requires small steps for stability; appropriate for simple real-time targets with tight compute budgets.

tools.name: ode3
tools.description: Fixed-step explicit Bogacki-Shampine (third-order) solver. It is the default fixed-step continuous solver and the default integration method of odeN.
tools.notes: A good balance between accuracy and cost for real-time simulation.

tools.name: ode4
tools.description: Fixed-step classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) solver, widely used for real-time and HIL plant models.
tools.notes: Four derivative evaluations per step.

tools.name: ode5
tools.description: Fixed-step fifth-order Dormand-Prince solver: the fixed-step counterpart of ode45's formula.
tools.notes: Six derivative evaluations per step.

tools.name: ode8
tools.description: Fixed-step eighth-order Dormand-Prince solver for very accurate fixed-step integration of smooth problems.
tools.notes: High cost per step; only pays off when the solution is very smooth.

tools.name: ode14x
tools.description: Fixed-step implicit solver combining Newton's method with extrapolation, for stiff models that must run with a fixed step (e.g. real-time Simscape models). ode1be (backward Euler with a fixed number of Newton iterations) is a cheaper implicit alternative.

parameters.name: ExtrapolationOrder
parameters.description: Extrapolation order 1-4.

parameters.name: NumberNewtonIterations
parameters.description: Newton iterations per step.

tools.notes: Computes a Jacobian, so cost grows with the number of states.

tools.name: StopTime (model parameter)
tools.description: Simulation stop time in seconds (StartTime gives the start). 'inf' runs until stopped by the user, a Stop Simulation block or an external mode disconnect.

parameters.name: StartTime
parameters.description: Default '0.0'.

parameters.name: StopTime
parameters.description: Default '10.0'; accepts expressions and 'inf'.

tools.notes: Both are strings evaluated in the model workspace; for sweeps prefer SimulationInput setModelParameter.

tools.name: RelTol (model parameter)
tools.description: Relative tolerance of variable-step solvers: the local error of each state must be below RelTol times the state magnitude (or AbsTol). Tighten it when results change with the tolerance.
tools.notes: A convergence check (repeat with 10x tighter tolerance) is the standard way to validate accuracy.

tools.name: AbsTol (model parameter)
tools.description: Absolute tolerance of variable-step solvers, which dominates when states are near zero. 'auto' starts at 1e-6 and adapts to the maximum state magnitudes; blocks such as Integrator can override it per state.

parameters.name: AutoScaleAbsTol
parameters.description: 'on' scales the absolute tolerance to state magnitudes.

tools.notes: Set small absolute tolerances for states with tiny nominal values (e.g. charges in coulombs).

tools.name: MaxStep (model parameter)
tools.description: Largest step a variable-step solver may take ('auto' = (StopTime-StartTime)/50). Limit it to avoid stepping over short pulses or to get smoother logged output. MinStep and InitialStep bound the other end.

parameters.name: MinStep
parameters.description: Smallest allowed step; with MaxConsecutiveMinStep controls errors on repeated violations.

parameters.name: InitialStep
parameters.description: First step size guess.

tools.notes: A very small MaxStep turns a variable-step solver into an expensive fixed-step one; use Refine or decimation for smoother plots instead.

tools.name: FixedStep (model parameter)
tools.description: Step size of fixed-step solvers (the fundamental sample time). 'auto' chooses the greatest common divisor of the discrete sample times, or (StopTime-StartTime)/50 for purely continuous models.
tools.notes: All discrete sample times must be integer multiples of FixedStep.

tools.name: ZeroCrossAlgorithm (model parameter)
tools.description: Selects the zero-crossing location algorithm of variable-step solvers: 'Nonadaptive' (default, brackets each crossing precisely) or 'Adaptive' (adjusts tolerance to avoid excessive chattering). ZcThreshold sets the detection threshold for the adaptive algorithm.

parameters.name: ZeroCrossControl
parameters.description: 'UseLocalSettings', 'EnableAll' or 'DisableAll' zero-crossing detection.

parameters.name: ZcThreshold
parameters.description: Signal threshold, 'auto' or a positive number.

tools.notes: Use Adaptive for models whose signals chatter around zero (e.g. friction, switching).

tools.name: MaxConsecutiveZCs (model parameter)
tools.description: Maximum number of consecutive zero crossings (each within a very small time interval) before Simulink reports a diagnostic. It detects Zeno-like chattering that would otherwise make simulation crawl.

parameters.name: MaxConsecutiveZCsMsg
parameters.description: 'none', 'warning' or 'error' when the limit is exceeded.

parameters.name: ConsecutiveZCsStepRelTol
parameters.description: Relative time tolerance defining 'consecutive'.

tools.notes: Instead of raising the limit, fix chattering with hysteresis, the Adaptive algorithm or disabling zero-crossing on the offending block.

tools.name: AlgebraicLoopMsg (model parameter)
tools.description: Diagnostic for algebraic loops (direct-feedthrough cycles): 'none', 'warning' (default) or 'error'. Setting 'error' in production models forces loops to be broken explicitly with a delay or Memory block.

parameters.name: ArtificialAlgebraicLoopMsg
parameters.description: Diagnostic for loops introduced by atomic subsystems or model references.

tools.notes: Algebraic loops slow simulation and prevent code generation in many targets.

tools.name: AlgebraicLoopSolver (model parameter)
tools.description: Chooses the nonlinear solver Simulink uses to solve algebraic loops during simulation: 'TrustRegion' (robust default) or 'LineSearch' (can be faster for some loops).
tools.notes: Only affects simulation; generated code does not solve algebraic loops.

tools.name: EnableMultiTasking (model parameter)
tools.description: Treat each discrete rate as a separate task ('on', multitasking) or run all rates in one task ('off', single-tasking). Multitasking reflects preemptive real-time execution and requires Rate Transition blocks between rates.

parameters.name: AutoInsertRateTranBlk
parameters.description: 'on' automatically inserts hidden rate transitions where needed.

parameters.name: SampleTimeConstraint
parameters.description: 'Unconstrained', 'Specified' (with SampleTimeProperty) or 'STIndependent'.

tools.notes: Only meaningful for fixed-step solvers. Generated code gets one step function per rate when multitasking.

tools.name: SimulationMode (model parameter)
tools.description: How the model executes: 'normal' (interpreted), 'accelerator' (compiled C for the model), 'rapid-accelerator' (standalone executable, fastest for repeated runs), 'software-in-the-loop (sil)' and 'processor-in-the-loop (pil)' (run generated production code on host or target) or 'external' (connect to code running on hardware).
tools.notes: Accelerator modes need a C compiler; SIL/PIL need Embedded Coder. Model blocks have their own SimulationMode for referenced models.

tools.name: FastRestart (model parameter)
tools.description: Keeps the model compiled between simulations so that repeated runs (parameter sweeps, optimisation) skip compilation and initialisation. Only tunable parameters and inputs may change while it is on.
tools.notes: Structural edits are blocked while Fast Restart is on. parsim/batchsim use 'UseFastRestart','on' instead.

tools.name: ExtMode (model parameter)
tools.description: Includes external mode support in generated code so that Simulink can connect to the application running on target hardware, tune parameters and stream signals to scopes and dashboards live. Set SimulationMode to 'external' to connect.

parameters.name: ExtModeTransport
parameters.description: Transport layer index (e.g. TCP/IP or serial).

parameters.name: ExtModeMexArgs
parameters.description: Connection arguments such as IP address and port.

tools.notes: Hardware support packages (Arduino, Raspberry Pi) wrap this as 'Monitor & Tune' on the Hardware tab.

tools.name: AssertControl (model parameter)
tools.description: Model Verification block enabling: globally enables or disables all Assertion and Check blocks, or leaves each block's own Enable assertion setting in charge.
tools.notes: Located in Configuration Parameters > Diagnostics > Data Validity.

tools.name: DataTypeOverride (model parameter)
tools.description: Overrides fixed-point and floating-point data types in a model or subsystem with double, single or scaled double during simulation, for example to collect ideal ranges before fixed-point conversion. MinMaxOverflowLogging controls range instrumentation.
tools.notes: Normally managed by the Fixed-Point Tool; remember to reset it, as an active override silently changes model behaviour.

tools.name: UpdateModelReferenceTargets (model parameter)
tools.description: Rebuild policy for model reference simulation and code-generation targets: 'IfOutOfDate' (default, rebuild when known dependencies change), 'IfOutOfDateOrStructuralChange' or 'Force'.
tools.notes: Marked to be removed in a future release; it now sits under Advanced parameters on the Model Referencing pane.

tools.name: Math and Data Types pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane for simulation behaviour of math operations and data types: the default type for underspecified signals, net-slope computation for fixed point, and the application lifespan used to size timers.
tools.usage: Configuration Parameters > Math and Data Types; get_param/set_param on the model or its configuration set

parameters.name: DefaultUnderspecifiedDataType
parameters.description: 'double' or 'single' for signals whose type cannot be inferred.

parameters.name: UseDivisionForNetSlopeComputation
parameters.description: Net-slope computation strategy for fixed-point multiply/divide.

parameters.name: ApplicationLifespan
parameters.description: Expected run time in days ('inf' default) used to size absolute-time counters.

tools.notes: Single-precision defaults help when targeting processors without double-precision FPUs.

tools.name: Diagnostics pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane (with sub-panes Solver, Sample Time, Data Validity, Type Conversion, Connectivity, Compatibility, Model Referencing, Stateflow) where each check can be set to 'none', 'warning' or 'error'. Tightening diagnostics catches modelling mistakes early.

parameters.name: UnconnectedInputMsg / UnconnectedOutputMsg / UnconnectedLineMsg
parameters.description: Unconnected ports and lines.

parameters.name: IntegerOverflowMsg / SignalRangeChecking
parameters.description: Integer overflow on wrap/saturate and out-of-range signals.

parameters.name: ArrayBoundsChecking
parameters.description: Array index out of bounds in S-functions and MATLAB code.

parameters.name: InheritedTsInSrcMsg / MultiTaskRateTransMsg
parameters.description: Sample time inheritance in sources and unsafe rate transitions.

tools.notes: Results appear in the Diagnostic Viewer. Model Advisor checks recommend settings per safety standard.

tools.name: Hardware Implementation pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane describing the target hardware board and processor: word sizes, byte order and integer rounding that simulation emulates and code generation targets.

parameters.name: HardwareBoard
parameters.description: Board from an installed support package, e.g. 'Arduino Uno', 'Raspberry Pi', or 'None'.

parameters.name: ProdHWDeviceType
parameters.description: Device vendor->type, e.g. 'Intel->x86-64 (Windows64)', 'ARM Compatible->ARM Cortex-M'.

parameters.name: ProdEqTarget / TargetHWDeviceType
parameters.description: Whether the test hardware equals the production hardware, and the test device.

tools.notes: Wrong device settings lead to integer size mismatches between simulation and generated code.

tools.name: Model Referencing pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane controlling how a model behaves when referenced: allowed number of instances, rebuild policy, dependency tracking and whether root inputs are passed by reference.

parameters.name: ModelReferenceNumInstancesAllowed
parameters.description: 'Single', 'Multi' or 'Zero' instances of this model in a hierarchy.

parameters.name: ModelDependencies
parameters.description: Extra files the model depends on (for rebuild checks).

parameters.name: UpdateModelReferenceTargets
parameters.description: Rebuild policy (see its own entry).

tools.notes: Multi-instance models generate reusable code with instance data passed as arguments.

tools.name: Simulation Target pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane for the simulation build used by MATLAB Function blocks, Stateflow charts, C Caller and accelerator modes: custom C code to include, source files, libraries and parsing of custom code.

parameters.name: SimCustomHeaderCode / SimCustomSourceCode
parameters.description: Code inserted into the generated simulation target.

parameters.name: SimUserSources / SimUserIncludeDirs / SimUserLibraries
parameters.description: Additional source files, include folders and libraries.

parameters.name: SimParseCustomCode
parameters.description: 'on' parses custom code so C Caller blocks can list its functions.

tools.notes: Code generation uses the parallel Code Generation > Custom Code settings unless configured to reuse these.

tools.name: Code Generation pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane (Simulink Coder / Embedded Coder) selecting the system target file, language, toolchain, build configuration, report and code interface options for slbuild.

parameters.name: SystemTargetFile
parameters.description: 'grt.tlc', 'ert.tlc', 'autosar.tlc', 'slrealtime.tlc', ...

parameters.name: GenCodeOnly / GenerateReport / LaunchReport
parameters.description: Generate without compiling and produce the HTML code report.

parameters.name: Toolchain / BuildConfiguration
parameters.description: Compiler toolchain and 'Faster Builds', 'Faster Runs', 'Debug' or 'Specify'.

parameters.name: CodeInterfacePackaging
parameters.description: 'Nonreusable function', 'Reusable function' or 'C++ class'.

parameters.name: DefaultParameterBehavior
parameters.description: 'Tunable' or 'Inlined' (Optimization sub-pane).

tools.notes: Changing SystemTargetFile swaps in target-specific sub-panes; set it before other code generation options.

tools.name: Coverage pane
tools.description: Configuration Parameters pane (Simulink Coverage) that enables coverage collection during simulation and chooses metrics, scope and where results are saved.

parameters.name: CovEnable
parameters.description: 'on' collects coverage.

parameters.name: CovMetricStructuralLevel
parameters.description: 'BlockExecution', 'Decision', 'ConditionDecision' or 'MCDC'.

parameters.name: CovSaveSingleToWorkspaceVar / CovSaveName
parameters.description: Store cvdata in the SimulationOutput.

tools.notes: See the CovEnable (model parameter) entry for scripted reporting with cvhtml.
